title: Code Mode: Let the Code do the Talking - Sunil Pai, Cloudflare
talk_summary: Sunil Pai argues that instead of exposing hundreds of tools via JSON tool-calling, agents should generate code that runs in a capability-restricted sandbox against a typed API surface, collapsing many round-trips into one execution. He shows Cloudflare's 2,600-endpoint API exposed as just two tools (search + execute) cutting first-call context from ~1.2M tokens to ~1,000, and describes a harness architecture of sandboxed code execution with explicitly granted capabilities and full observability.

takeaways.technique: Two-tool search+execute over a typed API instead of one tool per endpoint
takeaways.what_they_do: Expose only 'search' (takes code, receives the OpenAPI spec) and 'execute' (runs generated code against discovered functions) rather than a tool per API endpoint.
takeaways.evidence_quote: he exposes just two tool calls. Uh search and execute. Both of these endpoints accept code as an input
takeaways.numbers: ~2,600 endpoints, ~1.2-1.5M tokens first call reduced to ~1,000 tokens (~99.9% reduction)

takeaways.technique: Collapse multi-step tool loops into one code execution
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of N sequential model round-trips for each API call, the model emits one script that loops, paginates, sequences and parallelizes calls in a single run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Instead, the model can generate this string of code, run it immediately right next to the API surface, and do it in one shot.
takeaways.numbers: ~8 round trips for the equivalent MCP flow vs one execution

takeaways.technique: Capability-based sandbox: start with zero capabilities, grant explicitly
takeaways.what_they_do: Run generated code in a fast-starting isolate that can only execute code by default; network fetches and APIs are granted explicitly, with all outgoing fetches controllable and fully observable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you start with something that has no capabilities. The only thing it can do is execute code. ... And then you grant capabilities to it explicitly.

takeaways.technique: Typed API surface + syntax/type errors as feedback
takeaways.what_they_do: Give the model a typed API so it gets type checking and syntax errors as machine-readable feedback, leveraging its large code training rather than JSON schema wrangling.
takeaways.evidence_quote: with code, you get a typed API, you can do type checking, there are syntax errors

takeaways.technique: Agent-facing DX: markdown docs, actionable errors, search discoverability
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat agents as the primary API consumer: docs in markdown, error messages that tell the agent what to do next, and search-based discoverability of capabilities.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Docs which are markdown, uh errors that let the agent know what to do next, uh discoverability via search.

takeaways.technique: Full observability/replay of executed agent code
takeaways.what_they_do: Require absolute observability into the sandbox so any past action can be traced back to the exact code that caused it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You need to know why last Tuesday it made a trade for $2.3 million ... You need to go back to that code. Absolute observability
